text:
jess: Heads up — noticed dashboard frame drops in canary today around 11:23 UTC. Heatmap + timeline stutter, main-thread locky. @mike @olivia https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/3367895432 :eyes:

mike: Which canary group? repro steps?

jess: Canary group `dashboard-v2-canary`. Repro: open dashboard -> set 30d range -> hover heatmap -> pan timeline. Chrome trace attached. Logs showed repeat kv-cache misses + route quota timeouts:

```
[warn] kv-cache: miss for key heatmap:123
[info] route-quota: token_acquire_timeout=500ms
[debug] prefetch.queue.size=18
```

olivia: I remember a similar spike in prod on Wed — prefetch queue backed up and client started serializing fetches. When route quota kicks in we end up with cascading stalls.

samir: Looking at our distributed traces, kvcache RPC p95 jumps to ~230ms during the spike. Client code currently serializes when `missCount > 10` to avoid thundering herd, which ends up blocking main thread rendering.

nisha: Telemetry shows sampling for `route=dashboard` spiked from 2% -> 100% around the same time (we rolled a sampler change last week). That increased observed load on the fallback path.

jess: Chrome long-task snapshot (snippet):

```
LongTask 1202ms - main (parseHTML -> v8 run -> requestAnimationFrame blocked)
  at renderHeatmap (dashboard.js:45)
  at onHover (dashboard.js:120)
```

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 3340000000 -> 3349999999 started at 3367891200 by @release-bot :rocket:

mike: Short-term mitigation: relax route quota for the canary (increase tokens) or flip `route.policy.concurrent_prefetch=true` for canary to allow some parallelism. Command to toggle:

`redwoodctl config set route.policy.concurrent_prefetch true --scope=canary`

olivia: We can flip concurrent_prefetch, but it will increase pressure on kvcache. Safer short term is bumping token pool in eu-west-1 and throttling sampler back down.

samir: Longer term we should avoid client-side serial fallback. Server-side aggregation for small heatmap tiles would remove the main-thread work when cache misses spike. Also add circuit-breaker to stop client prefetch if route quota timeouts exceed X.

jess: I rolled back the canary to previous variant. Frame drops disappeared in canary within minutes. I'll open a follow-up RFC for server-side aggregation + quota autoscaling.

mike: Thanks. Can someone create a short incident note? Tagging @nisha for the telemetry rollout changes. :thumbsup:
